verdicts.reason: Quote says start bit starts at edge E0, i.e. first cycle after handshake; rule is fine. Actor is the transmitter, not master; kept as-is for actor since the interface role is ambiguous. Checkable from o_txd and handshake.
Quote states frame length 10N and stop bit ending at E0+10N; checkable from o_txd.
Quote directly states o_tx_ready timing: 0 for 10N-1 cycles, 1 in last stop-bit cycle; checkable on interface.
Quote states the block never drops an offered byte while o_tx_ready=0; needs data-tracking scenario, not a per-cycle assertion.
REQ-TIM-001 states back-to-back acceptance every 10N cycles; checkable both ways.
REQ-TIM-002 states in-order transmission; needs scoreboard scenario.
Quote states delivery latency V = T0+H+9N+2; checkable by timing.

Quote describes the smallest spacing between detected start bits as a property and tolerance consequence; it is descriptive, and the rule's 'must detect start bit at smallest spacing' is not what the quote states precisely.
REQ-TIM-003 states back-to-back frame acceptance; exercisable by scenario.
Quote states overrun pulse for one cycle and held byte unchanged when full and i_rx_ready=0 at V; checkable on interface.

questions.question: Are 'master' and 'slave' the correct actor labels for the UART transmitter and receiver? UL-8.1-xx and UL-8.2-xx describe a transmitter and a receiver, not bus master and slave roles.
UL-8.1-01 says the start bit starts at E0 and also that this is the first cycle after the handshake. Is the start bit visible on o_txd during the cycle that follows E0, or is it visible at E0 itself?
UL-8.1-03 says o_tx_ready is 0 for 10N-1 cycles after E0. Does it go back to 1 in the last cycle of the stop bit, which would mean the handshake lets the next byte be accepted at E0+10N?
What are H and M? The quotes don't define H, the half-bit offset, or M, the stop-bit sample point. For odd N, how is H rounded?
